summary: Live dashboard query hangs during usage export when tracehook-enabled filters are applied
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLane Health reports that exporting usage CSV from a live dashboard with an active tracehook filter causes the query to hang indefinitely and the UI to show "Export in progress..." with no progress for >30 minutes. Export never completes and the download link is never produced.

Impact:
- Affects one BrightLane Health org on dedicated capacity in us-east.
- Customers cannot generate ad-hoc usage exports that include tracehook-scoped filters; blocks several compliance reporting workflows.
- Multiple export requests spin up long-running queries that increase load on query-engine and occasionally push autoscaler into higher CPU usage.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (prod) connected to BrightLane Health dedicated cluster (us-east).
- Affected route: /orgs/{org}/dashboards/{id}/export-usage
- Query engine: analytics-query-v3 behind console-api gateway.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login to BrightLane Health account in prod (us-east) and open the live dashboard with usage widget.
2) Apply a tracehook filter (e.g., tracehook:service="ingest-proxy") and set a multi-day timespan (7d).
3) Click "Export CSV" on the usage widget and select "Include tracehook context".
4) Observe the UI spinner persists; backend export job shows status "running" for >30 minutes.
5) Check console-api logs and analytics-query-v3 slow query traces.

Observed logs / snippets:
- console-api: "export-job 0x7f3a: enqueue -> dispatched to query-engine job=export-7890"
- query-engine: "query-id=export-7890 status=running duration=1800s plan=Filter(TraceHook) -> Exchange -> Aggregate"
- query-engine: repeated GC/parallel-scan stalls and no rows returned.

Initial workaround:
- Customer can uncheck "Include tracehook context" and export succeeds.
- Alternatively, narrowing timespan to <24h allows export to complete successfully.

Notes:
- This does not appear to be a permissions/RBAC issue. Exports without tracehook filters complete normally.
- Multiple similar but not identical tickets exist for tracehook-related export edge cases (referenced in linked_issues).

Requested outcome:
- Priority investigation to identify root cause and either provide a short-term mitigation (UI validation or server-side fast-fail) and longer-term fix in analytics-query-v3.

investigation_notes: Repro run in perf harness reproduced hang consistently when tracehook filter matched >200k unique trace ids across 7d range.
Flame graphs show 65% CPU time spent in exchange/merge nodes and blocking network shuffle. Memory spikes precede stalls.
Query planner currently applies TraceHook filter after a distributed aggregation stage; moving it earlier reduces intermediate data by ~98% in tests.
Export job queue metrics: peak concurrent export jobs for BrightLane = 18 at time of incident; after rate-limit mitigation reduced to 3.
No immediate signs of corrupted index or missing partition metadata; root cause is planner ordering and lack of export fast-fail threshold.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: applied org-level concurrent export cap for BrightLane Health (3 concurrent exports). Communicated to customer 2026-03-12 08:10.
Engineering patch PR #2312 implements tracehook predicate pushdown and adds cardinality-based fast-fail for export jobs. Landing in main after QA.
Planned rollout: canary to staging 2026-03-13, canary to us-east dedicated cluster 2026-03-15, full rollout 2026-03-17 pending no regressions.
Customer follow-up: CS to schedule a post-deploy validation window with BrightLane for their weekly scheduled export on 2026-03-18 and confirm resolution.
Postmortem action items: add automated test for tracehook-filtered exports with large-cardinality ranges; add exporter-side queue monitoring alert (SLO: export queue depth <5 per org).
